summary: Analysis/source only; no Lean, no computation. Two corrections. (1) H translates each GIVEN finite POINT SET with its coordinates FIXED - no rotation, no re-realisation - so 'can this graph be realised inside the domain' is a different criterion. A horizontal strip of width w therefore fails H trivially: F = {0, (w+1)i} has vertical separation w+1 invariant under translation, so no translate fits; two points, no edges, no rigidity needed. The rigidity claim for a triangulated triangular-lattice disk is WITHDRAWN as unsupported and unnecessary. (2) Prepared the minimal local-check packet check_null_transfer.lean: 142 lines, 0 sorry/admit/elisions, ONE import (OAI.Geometry.PlaneColoring.Coloring, a leaf whose only import is Mathlib, supplying the exact in-tree ProperColoring), a private namespace NullTransferCheck, and two #print axioms. It contains the finite-compactness step extracted verbatim from Converse.lean:33 (mechanically verified byte-identical after ':= by') plus the null-transfer proof transcribed from NullSetRobust.lean:20 with Fin 5 -> Fin k (diff shows only two deliberate renamings to avoid variable capture). Conclusions are stated in terms of the qualified in-tree predicate, so correspondence is definitional. All assumptions preserved; the conclusion is existence, not extension. Five and no_proper_five_coloring neither imported nor reproved. This is extraction, not a new theorem claim; both files remain UNCOMPILED.

verified_results.statement: Correction: H quantifies over translations of a GIVEN finite point set with coordinates fixed. Rotating a configuration, or choosing a different realisation of a graph, is a different criterion and must not be used to assess H.

verified_results.statement: A horizontal strip S = {z : |Im z| <= w/2} fails H, trivially: F = {0, (w+1)i} has vertical separation w+1, invariant under translation, so F + t is never contained in S. Two points, no unit edges, no rigidity argument.
